documents_checked.text:
Principle 4: Privacy protection and security
Comply with applicable data protection, security and privacy policies and
legislation. Adhere to the University’s architecture standards if incorporating
AI systems into the University’s enterprise information technology systems.
Principle 5: Reliability and safety
Operate AI systems in accordance with the approved and intended purpose
and monitor their performance. Adopt safety measures proportionate to the
magnitude of potential risks.
Principle 6: Transparency, Explainability and Contestability
Develop, deploy and use AI systems in a way that maximises transparency,
explainability and contestability. Allow stakeholders to know when AI has
been used and contest decisions made using AI.
Principle 7: Accountability
Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Purpose-bounded authorisation for combined standing powers, with security, intervention and contestability of consequential actions.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Curtin's governance is siloed across separate instruments (N001, N005/N006, N007, N011, N002) with no connected purpose-bounded authorisation, cross-system ownership, or operational intervention and contestability workflow for an AI agent exercising standing authority across LMS, student support, enrolment, advising, and assessment systems without per-action human review.
case_summary.case_note: Curtin mandates human oversight, intervention, and contestability for AI (N001), restricts ICT assets to authorised purposes (N005/N006), and assigns system-level access controls (N011). However, institutional ownership and oversight remain siloed across separate policies without purpose-bounded authorisation or connected intervention/contestability for an agent with standing powers across LMS, enrolment, advising, support, and assessment (D5=2, Critical gap=Yes). Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

Implement human oversight, review and the ability to intervene for all AI-
based functions and decisions. Identify the individual accountable for any
decision made using AI. Maintain records on the use of AI to comply with
recordkeeping obligations.
